_source.description: Metastasis to the brain occurs in a significant fraction of patients with breast cancer and lung cancer (1-3). We mined published RNA-sequencing and multiplexed gene expression data (4, 5), comparing primary and brain metastatic tumor transcriptomes for the discovery of genes associated with metastasis to the CNS. We found that cluster of differentiation 6, encoded by CD6, was among the genes whose expression was most different in the brain metastases of patients with metastatic breast cancer as compared to primary tumors of the breast.  Multiplexed gene expression data (5) revealed conserved differential expression of CD6 in CNS metastasis in patients with lung cancer.  CD6 mRNA was present at decreased quantities in metastasis to the brain in humans with breast cancer.  Expression of CD6 in primary tumors of the breast was correlated with distant metastasis-free and recurrence-free survival.  Modulation of CD6 expression may be relevant to the biology by which tumor cells metastasize from the breast to the brain in humans with cancer of the lung and breast.

_source.title: CD6 is differentially expressed in central nervous system metastasis.
